Brethren of the Convention :�
Your Committee on the Annual Com
munication from the Executive Council beg leave to submit the following
partial report : (1.) In relation to the printing of the new Catalogue, your
Committee would report favorably on the suggestion of the Executive Coun
cil to leave the mode of printing with the Council. (2.) Your Committee
have thought it sufficient merely to call the attention of the Convention to the
inaccuracy in assigning the symbols by the Chapter officers, and, while effic
ient legislation by the Convention is deemed impracticable, would recommend
that greater care be taken in the future. (3.) Your Committee would report
favorably in regard to the suggestion of the Executive Council that copies of
the Amendments to the Constitution be furnished each of the Chapters.
(4.) Your Committee congratulates the Fraternity on the efficient services
rendered by the Zeta Chapter, in the compilation of the new Song Book, and
would recommend that each Chapter inform its graduate members where a
new edition of the same can be obtained. (5.) Your Committee would also
recommend that the report of progress by the Committee on the new Cata
logue be accepted. The problem of devising financial means for its early
publication has been referred to a special Committee.

PUBLIC LITERARY EXERCISES.
These exercises were held at the "
South Church,
"
which was finely decor
ated with flowers and tropical plants. Bro. M. B. Copeland {Xi), Cashier of
the M. National Bank, presided at the organ, and Bro. H. L. Osborn {Xi '78)
at the piano. Under the direction of Bro. G. E. Stockwell {Xi '78) the Fra
ternity sang "Gaudeamus," "Convention Song," "Suonila Tromba," and
the "Dianiond Song." His Excellency A. H. Rice, LL. D. {Theta '44), Gov.
of Mass., presided. He was one of the founders of the Psi and Alpha. The
prayer was by Prof. J. Strong, S. T. D. (Xi '44), of Drew Theological Semi
nary, author of many Biblical works, especially (with Dr. McClintock) of a
Cyclopeedia in 10 quarto volumes. He was Convention Orator in 1865. The
Poet, Prof. H. H. Boyesen, Ph. D. (Chi) of Cornell University, is the author of
"Gunnar," "A Norseman's Pilgrimage," and "Tales from Two Hemispheres."
The oration was by Gov. J. R. Hawley, LL. D. (Psi 47'), ex-Gov. of Ct., and
Pres't of the U. S. Centennial Commission. He was the Psi delegate to Con
vention held with the Xi 30 years ago, and was Convention Orator in 1869.
The Convention Song was by John G. Saxe, LL. D. (Alpha), set to music by
Prof. C. S. Harrington {Xi '52). At the Supper, given by the McDonough
House, Gov. Rice presided, and Prof. C. T. Winchester acted as Toastmaster.

THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION OF THE
EXECUTIVE COXJN^OIL
To the Forty-fourth Annual Convention of the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity :
The Executive Council presents its usual budget of facts and figures, and
makes certain suggestions relative to the legislative needs of the Fraternity.
1. Condition op the Chapters.�This year has passed very quietly
within the domain of Psi Upsilon. Harmony and prosperity have prevailed.
Although some chapters appear to have declined in numbers, we have no
evidence that they have lost in power or love for Psi U. The Iota Chapter,
unrepresented at the 43d Convention, has exhibited new vigor and an ex
cellent fraternity spirit. From one of our oldest and 'most revered Chapters
no "reports" have been received. In general, the Chapters have enjoyed their
usual prosperity.
2. The Chi Instituted. �
The petition for a
Chapter at the Cornell Uni
versity having been granted at the last Convention, the Chapters unani
mously ratified its action. On the 12th of June, 1876, the Chi Chapter was
formally instituted by Frederick G. Dow, Esq. (Kappa '72), Secretary of the
Executive Council. A new and excellent feature was the public exercises.
The Hon. William Taylor (r7iefa'38) presided; the Rev. Maunsell Van Rensselear, D. D., LL. D. (Theta '38) delivered an oration, and Professor, Henry
Webster Parker (Gamma '43) read a poem. The young Chapter by its zeal for
true Psi Upsilon principles has assumed a position in the Fraternity of
which, perhaps, it will not boast, but which should be highly appreciated by
all the other Chapters.
3. Printed Records.�The records of the last Convention were printed
at a very late date, not through the fault of the Recorder, but because- there
was not money in the treasury to pay for the printing. Please to decide upon
the accuracy of Gen. Res. No. 17. There is reason to believe that the first
clause is correct, but that the last clause was not enacted.
4. Amendments.�The Constitutional amendments adopted by the 43d
Convention and referred to the Chapters have been ratified. Two Chapters
voted. The rest failing to report action, were counted in the affirmative by
default. The Chapters are reminded that by this method�perfectly con
stitutional�they may sometime find, greatly to their chagrin, that an ob-
�noxious amendment has been incorporated into the Constitution, and solely
because of delay in acting upon matters referred to them. The Constitution
having now been amended eleven times, the Council suggests that measures
be taken to furnish each Chapter with a copy of them in such form as will be
convenient for reference.

14
5. Song Book.�During the year the new and enlarged edition of songs
has appeared. An expression of your appreciation of the services rendered
by the Zeta would be eminently fitting. If graduates were informed where
and how to obtain them, two or three hundred copies would doubtless be
ordered.
6. Catalogue.�
Work on the new catalogue has been the most absorb
ing labor of the year. At its first meeting the Council appointed Brother
Charles W. Smiley (Xi '74) to be General Editor. Your attention is called to

ARTICLE II.
All votes on the final passage of any resolution shall betaken by
chapters ; under all other circumstances voting, shall be viva voce ; provided,
however, that the yeas and nays shall always be taken when called for by
three delegates.
The general order of business at any session shall be : 1. Letters,
petitions, remonstrances, presented, or referred ; 2. Special Orders ; 3. Un
finished Business ; 4. General Business.
